questions.question: Explain the CSS box model — how do margin, border, padding, and width interact?
questions.title: Css Box Model
questions.direct_answer: Every element renders as a box: content (the text/inner size), padding (space INSIDE the border), border, and margin (space OUTSIDE, pushing neighbors away). The default is content-box: width sets only the CONTENT width, so the rendered size = width + padding + border (margin excluded). box-sizing: border-box makes width include padding+border — the declared width IS the visible width — which is why nearly all stylesheets set it globally.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph box
        M[margin - outside, transparent, collapses]
        B[border - the drawn edge]
        P[padding - inside, takes background]
        C[content - width x height]
    end
    M --> B --> P --> C
    CB[content-box: width = content only] -->|plus padding + border| R1[rendered = 250px]
    BB[border-box: width = content + padding + border] -->|declared = rendered| R2[rendered = 200px]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
Why border-box won (the history that explains the present): the CSS spec's original content-box made layout arithmetic painful — resize padding and every fixed-width element overflows its grid. The CSS3 box-sizing property let authors opt into the saner model; the universal-reset pattern (`*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box }`) became so universal that frameworks (Tailwind preflight, Bootstrap reboot) bake it in. Interviewers ask this because legacy content-box reasoning still bites in third-party CSS and email templates.

Margin collapse — the full rules (the depth marker): collapse happens (1) between adjacent siblings' vertical margins, (2) between a parent and its first/last child when no border/padding/inline content separates them — the child's margin can 'escape' through the parent, (3) between empty blocks' own top and bottom margins. Collapse does NOT happen: in flex/grid formatting contexts, horizontal margins ever, absolutely-positioned elements, or floats (with caveats). The debugging corollary: 'why is my parent offset by the child's margin?' is always collapse-through — the fixes are padding-top on the parent, overflow: hidden (a new BFC), or display: flow-root (the modern, purpose-built fix).

The measuring APIs (the runtime connection): getComputedStyle + getBoundingClientRect expose the resolved box. offsetWidth = border-box rendered width (content + padding + border, no margin); clientWidth = content + padding (no border, no margin); scrollWidth = clientWidth + overflowed content. Knowing which measures what is how you debug 'my measured width doesn't match my CSS width' — almost always a padding/border inclusion mismatch.
